data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test's guard is installed as part of the subject's own registry \u2014 if the guard lives in the same registry as the subject, the test and subject are mutually constraining, and the distinction between describing and constraining collapses.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the guard is outside the subject's registry but the mutation is still lost, the collapse is not necessary.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distribution is explained by one author and one week rather than registry structure, the mechanism is confounded.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the same registry produces different loss rates across modules, the registry is not the determining factor.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the shown-to-fail-first installation is removed and the loss rate changes, the registry is not sufficient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The registry is the point of collapse: when the guard and the subject share a registry, the test's failure mode is part of the subject's accepted vocabulary. The 1/9 mutation lost in compile.py suggests that the guard was keyed to the registry's declared data, so mutations that added behaviour outside the registry were not constrained. The 3-of-26 result reflects the registry size and the arbitrariness of what the registry includes.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
